title: Lech Lecha: new names (Genesis 17)
hook: Abram becomes Abraham, Sarai becomes Sarah, and the covenant of circumcision begins

segments.voice: Yesterday, the covenant between the pieces: count the stars, and a torch in the dark. Your line was the promise is long. Today, the last day of Lech Lecha, and two new names. Day one hundred seventy-five.

Think about the names you've been called in your life. The name on your birth certificate. The nickname from childhood you'd rather forget. The name your grandmother used. Maybe a name you chose for yourself, or one you took when you married, or converted, or just grew up. Names aren't only labels. They carry who you were, and sometimes who you're becoming. Abram is ninety-nine years old. He's been Abram his whole life. And God tells him that name is too small now. Today, how a name grows by a single letter.
screen: `THE NAMES YOU'VE BEEN CALLED.` → `WHO YOU WERE, WHO YOU'RE BECOMING.` → `A NAME GROWS BY ONE LETTER.`

segments.voice: God appears to Abram and says: walk before me, and be whole-hearted. Then: "Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for the father of a multitude of nations have I made thee." Abram means something like exalted father. Abraham is heard as av hamon goyim, father of a multitude of nations. The change is one Hebrew letter: a heh, added in the middle. Then Sarai. God says: don't call her Sarai any more; Sarah shall be her name. And she'll be blessed, and have a son, and be a mother of nations and kings. Sarai means my princess. Sarah means princess. The Talmud puts it this way: at first she was a princess only to her own people; now she's a princess for the whole world. The ending that meant mine is dropped. She stops belonging to one household and starts belonging to everyone. Her name also changes by one letter. The yod at the end becomes a heh. And the midrash notices that heh is a letter in God's own name. As if God gave each of them a piece of the divine name. The Talmud even says: anyone who calls Abraham by his old name, Abram, misses the point. The growth counts. The same chapter begins the covenant of circumcision, brit milah, for Abraham and his household, and for every Jewish boy on the eighth day. To this day, that's when a Jewish boy is named. A covenant and a name, given together. So that's Lech Lecha, finished. Go to yourself. Be a blessing. Not a thread. A long promise in the dark. And a name that grows.
screen: `ABRAM BECOMES ABRAHAM.` · `SARAI BECOMES SARAH.` · `ONE LETTER, FROM GOD'S NAME.` · `A COVENANT AND A NAME TOGETHER.` · then, large: `A NAME CAN GROW.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: say your own name with care. Settle, and breathe. Say your name silently, slowly, the way someone who loves you would say it. Notice what it carries: who named you, what it means, the people who've said it kindly. Then ask: who am I growing into? Imagine a letter added to your name, a small piece of something larger. Say your name once more, with that in it. The bell holds the time.
Lech Lecha. The portion that begins with go to yourself and ends with new names: Abraham, and Sarah.
Your line: a name can grow. Today, say someone's name with real care, and use the name they want to be called. Day one hundred seventy-five.

howItsDone: Jewish boys are named at their brit milah on the eighth day, and girls are often named in the synagogue at a Torah reading or at a naming ceremony; Jews are called to the Torah by their Hebrew names.

fork.reveal: Abraham: av hamon goyim, father of a multitude of nations. the name grows to fit the promise.

original.note: Hebrew: Abraham, heard as father of a multitude of nations.

trapdoor: what you thought: Abraham just had two versions of his name.
what it means: God renames Abram and Sarai to fit the promise, each by one letter, with a covenant at the same time.
what a scholar hears: the added heh (Genesis Rabbah 39:11; 47:1 on Sarai's yod); Berakhot 13a: Sarah a princess 'for all the world', and calling Abraham 'Abram' is a transgression.

sources.quoted: Neither shall thy name any more be called Abram, but thy name shall be Abraham; for the father of a multitude of nations have I made thee.

notes: Meaning of 'Abram' ('exalted father') is the usual gloss; confirm.

Berakhot 13a: 'at first a princess to her own people, in the end to all the world'; and 'whoever calls Abraham Abram transgresses'. The script softens 'transgresses' to 'misses the point'; confirm the softening is acceptable.
The heh from God's name: Genesis Rabbah (and Jerusalem Talmud Sanhedrin 2:6 on the yod of Sarai given to Joshua). Confirm citation.
Circumcision is described briefly and neutrally; girls' naming customs appear only in howItsDone.
